Support Ops: FYI we're getting a customer escalation — ~30% of their requests returning 503s starting ~09:12 UTC. Logs show upstream infer-worker exiting repeatedly. :rotating_light:
Support Ops: stacktrace snippets and docker exit codes attached, customer on hosted tier, model: llama-2-70b-q4 (quantized).
Support Ops: ```
[2026-03-17T09:12:05Z] infer-runner[pid:4217] SIGSEGV (code=139)
[2026-03-17T09:12:05Z] nvml: GPU 0 reset detected
[2026-03-17T09:12:06Z] container exit code 139 -> restarted by k8s
[2026-03-17T09:12:10Z] OOM-killer triggered: cgroup memory high
```
Maria Chen: I'm oncall for eng-runtime, looking. Any recent deploys to that pool?
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-17T09:05:12 by pipeline/runtime-swap completed -> image: infer-runner:v2026.03.17-rc4
Ben O'Neill: That canary touched the quantized swap path (q4 -> q2) for that model family — possible memory regression.
Alex Patel: Customer says first spike happened right after they sent a 5k token batch for reranking, sent a sample request in support ticket (attached). They saw timeouts then 503s.
Maria Chen: Can we get the full container stderr and nvml logs for GPU 0 on node ip-10-2-8-13? Also need pod spec (batch_size, max_context, prefetch enabled).
Support Ops: Pasted pod spec: ```
resources: nvidia.com/gpu: 1
args: [--max_context=8192, --batch-size=64, --kv-prefetch=true]
image: infer-runner:v2026.03.17-rc4
```
Ben O'Neill: batch-size=64 + max_context=8192 on q4 quant can push memory above headroom when KV prefetch is enabled. If kernel change in rc4 bumped resident set, that could cause SIGSEGV during memory alloc.
Maria Chen: Reproducing locally: running a single 5k token request with batch-size 16 repros OOM on my dev A100 when kv-prefetch=true and v2026.03.17-rc4 image used. With rc3 it works fine.
Ben O'Neill: Good repro. Steps for triage: 1) roll back canary on affected pool to v2026.03.16-rc12; 2) set kv-prefetch=false for this customer as an immediate mitigation; 3) collect gdb backtrace from the crashing runner.
Support Ops: Doing rollback now. kubectl rollout undo deployment/infer-runner --to-revision=2026.03.16-rc12 on pool-hosted-a
Support Ops: Also applied annotation to override kv-prefetch=false for the customer's route.
deploy-bot: Rollback started -> rollout id: rbo-5230012345-1
sre-bot: Node ip-10-2-8-13 restart_count=7 in last 12m, cpu: 65%, gpu_mem_used: 98% on GPU0
Alex Patel: Customer confirms partial recovery: errors drop to ~3% but still intermittent timeouts for large requests. They're asking about billing credits for impacted calls.
Maria Chen: We'll offer a credit; SRE/Support, please calculate from request logs between 09:12-09:40 UTC. Action items: eng-runtime to bisect rc4->rc3 changes to quant kernel selection and memory allocations; create a hotfix that avoids the changed allocation path.
Ben O'Neill: I found the likely diff: change in kv cache prefetch allocator and a small refactor in attention kernel that changed temporary buffer sizing. I'll prepare a branch with a guard for prefetch memory reservation.
Support Ops: For immediate product mitigation: 1) route heavy requests to a smaller model variant (llama-2-13b-q4) automatically via fallback policy for affected customers; 2) add a service-level rule to reject single requests > 4096 tokens for hosted pools until fix.
Maria Chen: Add repro checklist in the incident ticket: reproduction command, exact request payload, dev env A100 image, gdb backtrace path, and logs.
Support Ops: Repro command we used: ```
# run inside sample infra container
python reproduce.py --model llama-2-70b-q4 --context 5000 --batch 16 --kv-prefetch true
# collect gdb: gdb --batch --ex "thread apply all bt full" -p <pid> > /tmp/backtrace.txt
```
Alex Patel: Customer asked for ETA. I'll tell them "engineering is investigating, rollback applied, mitigation in place; expecting fix in next 6-12 hours" — is that accurate?
Maria Chen: Yes, set expectation 6-12h. Ben, how long for the guard branch and validation?
Ben O'Neill: I'll aim for a branch and CI run in 3h, staging validation after that, hotfix PR in ~6h. If CI passes we can ship a patched runner image and gradually roll it.
Support Ops: Logging follow-up: assigned incident #INC-2026-0317-07, created runbook entries for fallback config and token caps.
Maria Chen: Marking this thread for postmortem. Please attach timeline and root cause once available. :white_check_mark:
Support Ops: Closing slack thread — monitoring for 1h; will reopen if errors resurge.
